Before, 1 week, 2 week and 3 week are one score at four time points as columns, one row per subject ('One-way repeated measures ANOVA using a wide-format dataset', pg.rm_anova(data)); the source holds no long form, rm_anova.csv being other data.

Hits of At-Bats (BattingAverage) over each player's early at-bats and RemainingAverage over his RemainingAt-Bats are one batting record at two periods of the season as columns, one row per player, SeasonHits, SeasonAt-Bats and SeasonAverage their totals; the long form is player x period, and the notebook's Binomial with a per-player theta fits the first period alone.

pitcher_name indexes the pitchers whose average spin rate repeats over game_date, many games each, and MOGP-Coregion-Hadamard fits a multi-output Gaussian process with one output per pitcher (B = W W' + diag(kappa)); re-filed with pitcher_name against the first reading's GP rule.

the coordinates x and y identify the village ('our sample of 65 villages') whose children's rows repeat within it, and malaria_prevalence fits a binomial per village with a spatial HSGP intercept over those coordinates; re-filed with x:y, the coordinates a sampled unit's id and no field coordinate held once.

len8, len85, len9 and len95 are each boy's jaw bone length 'measured on four fixed occasions, at ages 8, 8.5, 9, and 9.5 years' (RAO.ASC), one row per boy; the source holds no long form, its RAO.WS worksheet the same four columns as OCC1 to OCC4.

art1 to art10 and cit1 to cit10 are each academic's articles and citations by year as columns, one row per academic (id); ch14.do builds the person-year long form by reshape long art cit, i(id) j(year) for its time-varying discrete-time hazard logit, and the source holds no long form.

GRS to BTS are the catch of each shark species code on one longline set, one measure repeated over species, one row per set with its own Lat and Lon and a two-level Zoning; the long form is set x species, while the book's chapter 5 fits GLMs to the tiger sharks, the total of all species and the silvertip sharks one at a time (https://www.highstat.com/Books/BGS/ZIM/pdfs/TOCOnly.pdf).

y1 to y4 are 'four repeated measurements of blood lead levels obtained at baseline (or week 0), week 1, week 4, and week 6' on each child (id), one row per child; the rows are the succimer arm of fitzmaurice_tlc's tlc.dta, filed wide, and no file holds a long form.
